name: Dub Your Video for a New Market
outcome: Translate your presenter clip into another language, with a new voice, lip-sync, and subtitle text.
audience: Teams localising demos, talks, and video ads.
summary: Keep the footage. Change the language. Transcribe your clip, translate the script, and generate a new voice track.
Review key messages with back-translations. Use the audio for a voice-over, or create a lip-synced presenter cut.
caveats: Lip-sync changes mouth movements. Gestures and on-screen text stay in the original language.
Translated speech may run longer than the source. Timing is not matched automatically.
Have a native speaker review tone and meaning before publishing.

apps.role: Transcribing writes the script into a field you can edit, and the revoice, subtitle and lip-sync steps all read what is in it.
Just the lip-sync step, for when the script is already settled and only the mouth has to match.

steps.handoff: Extract the spoken words as text. Only the audio goes to the transcription model.

steps.example: Localise a Script and Revoice It
steps.handoff: Choose a target language and turn the transcript into a new voice track.
Translate key lines into six languages, with back-translations for review.
Add the presenter clip and translated script. This step generates its own voice track and matches the mouth movements.
Turn the localised audio into text split into subtitle-length lines.
